query: A dedicated instance:

options.text: Can optionally run on multi-tenant hardware
Can only run in a dedicated VPC
Costs more than a non-dedicated instance

answer:
A dedicated instance only runs on single-tenant hardware. This means the physically hardware that supports the EC2 instance will not concurrently run any EC2 instances from other customers.

Since a dedicated instance removes a physical server from the AWS global resource pool, there are cost implications to Amazon. As a result, a dedicated instance is more expensive than a non-dedicated one.

While all EC2 instances that run in a dedicated VPC are themselves dedicated instances, it is possible to run a dedicated instance in a VPC that is not configured for single-tenancy.

query: Which of the following are true about both dedicated instances and dedicated hosts?

options.text: Both provide visibility for sockets, cores and host IDs
Both enable the use of dedicated physical servers
Both ensure affinity between the physical host and the instance
Both can perform automatic instance placement

answer:
Only a dedicated host allows for an ensured affinity between the physical host and the instance. Furthermore, only a dedicated host provides visibility into physical hardware components such as cores, sockets and host IDs.

When an dedicated instance or dedicated host is used, there is a physical sever in the AWS data center that is dedicated to you and only you.

Regardless of whether a dedicated host or dedicated instance is used, automatic EC2 instance placement will occur.

Dedicated Hosting

query: Your company wants to perform a full migration to the cloud. However, the company has 5 years outstanding on a WebSphere Portal Server contract that states the software is licensed to run on eight physical CPUs. Which of the following is the recommended option:

options.text: Renegotiate the Portal Server contract to allow for EC2 hosting
Deploy the WebSphere Portal software in a dedicated EC2 instance
Deploy the WebSphere Portal software in a reserved EC2 instance and limit the CPU capacity to eight
Deploy the WebSphere Portal software to an EC2 Dedicated Host

answer:
Only a dedicated host allows for visibility down to the level of sockets, host IDs and physical CPU cores. According to the AWS documentation:

"Dedicated Hosts allow you to use your existing per-socket, per-core, or per-VM software licenses, including Windows Server, SQL Server, SUSE Linux Enterprise Server, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, or other software licenses that are bound to VMs, sockets, or physical cores, subject to your license terms. "

query: Healthcare, Banking and Government compliance requirements often demand that computations be performed on a physical server that is not shared by any other users or organizations. Which is the best option to remain compliant with such regulations?

options.text: Implement a hybrid-cloud where regulated computations are performed in a local data center
Perform all regulated computations on an EC2 instance protected by AWS GuardDuty
Route all regulated computations to a regulatory compliant EC2 instance using an API Gateway
Run all regulated computations on a single-tenant, physical machine set up as a Dedicated Host

answer:
There is no need to implement a hybrid cloud to say compliant with regulations that demand operations happen on an isolated, physical machine. In such cases, simply allocate an AWS Dedicated Host and run the computations on this host. <.p>

A Dedicated Host is a single-tenant physical machine that is not shared with any other customers.

An API Gateway will not assist in solving this problem whatsoever.

Amazon GuardDuty provides threat detection. GuardDuty will monitor for malicious bugs, sneaky trojans, spyware, malware and incoming attacks. It's a great product, but it won't help provide government compliance through dedicated hardware. You need an AWS Dedicated Host for that.

query: AWS License Manager, which helps you manage software licensed based on a per-socket, per-CPU or per-VM basis, is fully integrated with which product offering?
answer:
Whenever a certification questions asks about per-CPU or per-socket licenses, the answer will almost always be the EC2 Dedicated Host. The dedicated host helps users run software that is licensed at the CPU, socket or VM level, something that is otherwise difficult to account for in the cloud.

To assist with the management of licenses used by an EC2 Dedicated Host, Amazon provides a complimentary AWS License Manager with all EC2 Dedicated Host configurations.

AWS Budgets is not used to manage licenses. It helps set alerts for when AWS costs are exceeded.

query: Quebec privacy laws forbid businesses to export and process any personally identifiable data outside of the borders of Quebec. Quebec based business that want to migrate to AWS, but also wish to process customer data, should:

options.text: Set up a hybrid-cloud configuration and process all personally identifiable information in a local data center
Limit processing of personally identifiable data to servers in the Montreal, QC Edge location
Limit processing of personally identifiable data to severs in the Canada Central Region (located in Monteal, QC)
Perform all data processing on an EC2 Dedicated Instance

answer:
Quebec has very strict privacy laws that forbid any personal data to be exported beyond Quebec's borders. Any data protected by privacy legislation must be processed in Quebec.

An important part of designing an AWS architecture is paying attention to privacy laws, data export legislation and data sovereignty regulations. To deal with Quebec's privacy laws, an organization could limit all processing to the new (2019) Canada Central Region located in Montreal. Or, they could optionally set up a hybrid cloud where personally identifiable data is processed in-house.

Both of these options are viable solutions to the privacy requirements of the province.

query: Which of the following is true about Standard Reserved Instances:

options.text: Standard Reserved Instances have the highest discount compared to On-Demand and Convertible
Standard Reserved Instances will benefit from EC2 price reductions that occur over the life of the term
Standard Reserved Instances cannot switch from muti-tenancy to single tenancy throughout the life of the term
Standard Reserved Instances cannot switch their underlying operating system throughout the life of the term

answer:
Standard Reserved Instances are cheap compared to On-Demand and Convertible instances. But that discount comes with a cost.

Standard Reserved Instances cannot take advantage of EC2 price reductions that happen during the length of the term.

Furthermore, Standard Reserved Instances do not allow the operating system, family, tenancy or payment option to change throughout the term. If any of these options are needed, choose a Convertible Reserved Instance.

query: To generate a cost estimate for the use of AWS services in multiple Regions with the AWS Pricing Calculator:

options.text: Create a multi-region group with the AWS Pricing Calculator and view the estimate
Add services to multiple Regions, enter your usage predictions and view the estimate
Use the AWS Pricing Calculator Region Aggregator function
You cannot generate an estimate for multiple Regions with the AWS Pricing Calculator

answer:
Sadly, you cannot generate an estimate with the AWS Pricing Calculator for multiple regions.

The best you can do is do a separate calculation for each region you are interested in and then add them together.

AWS Pricing Calculator only provides cost estimations for individual AWS Regions. To get a cost estimate for multiple AWS Regions, you must create a group for each Region, do the calculation, and then add them together.

query: Which tool is best suited to comparing AWS costs between Regions?
answer:
The purpose of the AWS Pricing Calculator is to help you estimate your costs of running AWS products in any way, shape or form. With AWS Pricing Calculator, you can easily compare the cost or running a product like Elastic Beanstalk in Asia as compared to North America.

AWS Budgets simply lets you set custom budgets that alert you when you start to spend more money than you anticipated.

AWS Cost Explorer is used to visualize and understand your current AWS costs. It doesn't do future estimates.

Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability management tool.

query: Which of the following are stated features of Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS)?

options.text: Easy to set up, operate and scale
Can be optimized for CPU, memory, storage or network capacity

answer:
The official documentation for Amazon RDS brags that the service makes it easy to set up, operate and scale a relational database in the cloud.

There are several RDS instance types that are optimized for CPU, memory, network I/O and storage.

As like most cloud products, Amazon RDS automates and simplified time-consuming administrative tasks. There's no installation or config needed. You just start the service and it's up and running!

Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a relational database in the cloud. It provides cost-efficient and resizable capacity while automating time-consuming administration tasks such as hardware provisioning, database setup, patching and backups.

You will need to create your own tables and schemas though. Amazon RDS doesn't know your data. Only you know your data. So you are the one who needs to create the tables, design the columns and fill in the fields.

Amazon RDS is a standard, old-school, relational database with tables, columns and fields.

Each of the other three options listed are types of NoSQL databases, which behave differently in terms of data replication, consistency, scalability and ACID compliance.

query: Which of the following are not stated benefits of Amazon RDS?

options.text: The ability to launch Read Replicas to offload query traffic
The ability to launch Write Replicas to offload transactional operations
Read Replicas can be promoted to a primary instance when needed to become a standalone DB
Write Replicas can be promoted to a primary instance when needed to become a standalone DB

answer:
Read operations can be performed significantly faster than transactional queries. For read-heavy workloads, or for highly transactional workloads where it makes sense to offload read operations away from the primary instance, Amazon RDS Read Replicas can be set up. This helps improve performance and minimize response times.

Another benefit to an RDS Read Replica is the fact that any Read Replica can be promoted to the primary instance if need be.

There is no such thing as a Write Replica.

query: Which AWS Service extends the benefits of Amazon RDS Read Replicas with a virtualized, SSD-backed storage layer?
answer:
One of the primary features of Amazon Aurora is to provide an SSD-backed storage layer for Amazon RDS Read Replicas.

Amazon Aurora replicas share the same underlying storage as the source instance, lowering costs and avoiding the need to copy data to the replica nodes.

According to the documentation, Amazon Aurora is up to five times faster than standard MySQL databases and three times faster than standard PostgreSQL databases. It provides the security, availability, and reliability of commercial databases at 1/10th the cost.

query: Which of the following statements are not true about Amazon RDS?

options.text: Amazon RDS cannot be deployed to multiple Availability Zones
Amazon RDS cannot be configured as a Multi-Region deployment
Read Replicas can be configured within an Availability Zone, Cross-AZ or Cross-Region
The main purpose of a Read Replica is high availability

answer:
The only true statement here is the fact that Read Replicas can be configured within an Availability Zone, Cross-Availability Zones and Cross-Region.

Relational database can get huge, so it just makes sense that Amazon RDS can be configured across multiple zones and regions.

According to the official documentation for Amazon RDS , the main purpose of a Read Replica is scalability.

Network connectivity to the primary database is lost
There is a compute unit or storage failure on the primary

answer:

  • Compute unit failure on primary
  • Loss of availability in primary Availability Zone
  • Loss of network connectivity to primary

query: Which of the following are benefits of using a managed service like Amazon RDS or DynamoDB?

options.text: Maintenance functions are performed without taking your DB instance offline
Amazon will make updates to the DB instance's underlying hardware
Amazon will make updates to the DB instance's underlying OS
Amazon will make updates to the DB instance's database engine version

answer:
A key benefit to using a managed AWS service like RDS or DynamoDB is the fact that AWS will upgrade the databsae engines, improve the underlying hardware and apply security patches. This greatly simplifies the management and administration of complex hardware and software.

Unfortunately, it is impossible to upgrade software and hardware without creating some type of an outage. However, Amazon does promise to keep these outages short.

Maintenance items that require a resource to be offline include required operating system or database patching. Required patching is automatically scheduled only for patches that are related to security and instance reliability. Such patching occurs infrequently (typically once every few months) and seldom requires more than a fraction of your maintenance window.

query: How can you tell if a maintenance update is available for your Amazon RDS DB instance?

options.text: Check the maintenance column in the RDS console
Check the online documentation about pending RDS DB patches and updates
Query the Amazon RDS DB instance's maintenance state with the AWS CLI
Query the Amazon RDS DB instance's maintenance state with Amazon RDS API

answer:
You can find out if an Amazon RDS maintenance update is available for your DB instance through the Amazon RDS API, the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or through the RDS console.

Online documentation may indicate a patch or update has become available. However, the online documentation will not tell you if the patch has or has not been applied to your Amazon RDS DB instance.

options.text: Amazon recommends Amazon RDS over Amazon EC2 for database deployments
Amazon recommends Amazon EC2 over Amazon RDS for database deployments
Amazon RDS can be configured with a synchronous secondary instance for failover, or with Read Replicas, but not both
Amazon RDS can be configured with both a synchronous secondary instance for failover and with Read Replicas

answer:
In most instances, Amazon says RDS is preferred over an Amazon EC2 instance configured with database software.

Amazon RDS can be configured with both a synchronous secondary instance and with Read Replicas, all at the same time. Organizations do not need to choose between the two configurations.

query: Which of the following statements are true?

options.text: EC2 is not a fully managed service
Databases run on Amazon EC2 are more prone to errors in comparison to services like Amazon RDS
OS patching is performed by AWS on EC2 instances
Database backups are performed by AWS when MariaDB is installed on EC2 instances

answer:
EC2 is not a fully managed service. The user must apply OS patches and backup any important files or databases that exist on the EC2 instance.

Databases installed on EC2 are more prone to errors in comparison to fully managed services like Amazon RDS, which is why Amazon recommends RDS over EC2 for databases.

query: Which of the following functions does the customer perform on EC2 instances?
answer:
According to the Amazondocumentation, on EC2 instances, the customer is tasked with optimization, scaling and OS patching. AWS takes care of all server maintenance.

It is worth noting that on both EC2 and RDS, Amazon always considers optimization to be the customer's job.

query: Which of the following statements are true about EC2 and RDS management

options.text: Application optimization is always the responsibility of the customer, never AWS
Application optimization is only the responsibility of the customer on EC2, not RDS
Scaling is always the responsibility of AWS, never the customer
Scaling is solely the responsibility of the customer on EC2, not RDS

answer:
Application optimization is the responsibility of the customer on both EC2 and RDS.

When it comes to scaling, it is the customer's job to figure out how to best scale EC2 instances. With Amazon RDS, how the system scales is the job of AWS.

query: How many custom CloudTrail trails can be made per region?

options.text: There is no limit to the number of custom trails that can be made per region

answer:
You can create up to 5 custom AWS CloudTrail trails per region.

From the docs:For example, a security administrator can create a trail that applies to all regions and configure encryption using one Amazon Key Management Service (KMS) key. A developer can create a trail that applies to one region for troubleshooting operational issues.

query: Which of the following would qualify as a CloudTrail Insight event?

options.text: Bursts of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) actions
Provide data protection in your account by discovering, classifying, and protecting sensitive data

answer:
CloudTrail Insights use AI and machine learning to discover anomalies in how your account is being used. Unusual resource provisioning, IAM actions or a lack of maintenance will all be flagged by CloudTrail insights.

The job of discovering, classifying, and protecting sensitive data is performed by Amazon Macie.

query: Which of the following are true about AWS CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail?

options.text: CloudTrail can use CloudWatch to raise alarms when unusual account activity occurs
CloudWatch can use CloudTrail to raise alarms when unusual account activity occurs
CloudTrail and CloudWatch are integrated together by default
CloudTrail and CloudWatch are not integrated together by default

answer:
CloudTrail is used to monitor AWS account activity. In contrast, CloudWatch is used to monitor applications and optimize resource utilization.

CloudWatch has alerting functionality, which CloudTrail can use if the two are integrated together. However, CloudWatch and CloudTrail are not integrated together by default. CloudWatch and CloudTrail integration must be performed explicitly by the user.

query: What level of annual durability does Amazon promise for AWS S3 Glacier?
answer:
AWS S3 annual durability is 99.999999999%, or 11 nines.

Some people thing the nines are counted after the decimal. That is not the case. The count includes the sum of the nines on both sides of the decimal.

If you do ever push this much data to a bucket, please use a multi-part loader.

query: Objects stored in a Standard S3 Bucket are automatically stored:

options.text: Across multiple devices in a single Availability Zone of your choosing
Across multiple devices spanning a minimum of two availability zones
Across multiple devices spanning a minimum of three availability zones

query: Which factors should go into choosing an AWS Region in which to store Amazon S3 data?

options.text: The selected region is close enough to permit an on-site inspection by your company's IT leadership
The selected region is near to your customers, your data centers, or your other AWS resources in order to reduce data access latencies
The selected region is remote from your other operations for geographic redundancy and disaster recovery purposes.
The selected region enables you to address specific legal and regulatory requirements of your country

answer:
An AWS Data Center is unlikely to ever be inspected by your corporate leadership.

Reducing latency, geographic redundancy, regulatory requirements and even reduced storage costs are all factors that go into picking an AWS Region.

query: Which of the following statements are true about Amazon S3?

options.text: Amazon S3 is a high-throughput, cloud-based block storage service
Amazon S3 is a high-throughput, cloud-based file system
Amazon S3 is a high-throughput, cloud-based object storage service
Amazon S3 is a high-throughput, cloud-based relational database service

answer:
According to the docs, Amazon S3 is object storage built to store and retrieve any amount of data from anywhere.

Do not confuse Amazon S3 with the Amazon Elastic File System (EFS), Amazon Elastic Block Storage (EBS) or Amazon's Relational Database Service (RDS).

answer:

Furthermore, if accounts are consolidated, the discount for reserved instances can be shared across accounts, which has the potential for great savings. Amazon wants you to know this interesting tidbit of information, and will likely ask you a question or two about it on the exam.

query: If two departments come together and start using AWS Organizations, which benefits will they accrue?

options.text: Root accounts will be able to share existing Reserved Instance discounts from another account
All accounts can share existing Reserved Instance discounts from another account
A single payment method can be used for all accounts
New AWS accounts can be created programmatically as the organization grows

answer:
There are two important exam objectives that deal with AWS Organizations, Consolidated Billing and Reserved Instances:

  • Describe Reserved-Instances behavior in AWS Organizations
  • Recognize that consolidated billing is a feature of AWS Organizations

Consolidated billing allows all accounts to combine their usage into a single bill. This is a key feature of AWS organizations that need to be understood for the exam.

Furthermore, if accounts are consolidated, the discount for reserved instances can be shared across accounts, which has the potential for great savings. Amazon wants you to know this interesting tidbit of information, and will likely ask you a question or two about it on the exam.

Note that the ability to share Reserved Instance discounts with AWS Organizations has nothing to do with root access.

AWS Organizations allows all managed accounts to be paid for with a single payment method.

AWS Organizations also allows for the programmatic creation of user accounts.

query: Which types of operating expenses (OpEx) can be reduced or eliminated as organizations move to the cloud?

options.text: Rent and property taxes paid on the data warehouse
Wages and salaries paid to workers managing on-site infrastructure
Cost of purchasing expensive servers and workstations
Cost of installing enterprise computing infrastructure such as high-speed fiber optic lines

answer:
Rent, property taxes, wages and salaries are all operating expenses (OpEx) that can be greatly reduced by a move to the cloud.

The cost of workstations and installing infrastructure can also be reduced as organizations move to the cloud, but these are CapEx costs, not OpEx.

Rent, taxes and utilities paid to support the on-site data warehouse
Cost of purchasing redundant servers and workstations to support failover
Cost of installing enterprise computing infrastructure such as high-speed fiber optic lines

The cost of backup servers and installing infrastructure will certainly be reduced as organizations move to the cloud. These are all considered capital expenditures (CapEx) costs.

query: Which of the following are true about the impact a move to the cloud has on an organization?

options.text: Variable costs become more predictable in the cloud than in an on-premises data center
Variable costs become less predictable in the cloud than in an on-premises data center
Upfront capital expenditures (CapEx) are small when an organization moves to the cloud
Upfront capital expenditures (CapEx) are large when organization moves to the cloud

answer:
A variable cost is one that changes in proportion to how much business a company does.

In the cloud, variable costs are highly predictable. In fact, it is very easy to calculate exactly how costs will vary as an organization services more clients in the cloud. That's exactly what tools like the AWS Calculator are used for. Variable costs in the cloud are completely predictable.

A move to the cloud also reduces upfront capital expenditures. Organizations do not have to spend tens of thousands of dollars on hardware and infrastructure in order to get online when using the cloud. In fact, organizations can start with a free-tier offering and scale up from there. Upfront capital expenditures don't get much less than zero!

options.text: Lower variable costs and lower upfront costs
Higher variable costs but lower upfront costs
Lower variable costs but higher upfront costs
Higher variable costs and higher upfront costs

answer:
More often than not, a move to the cloud will result in lower variable costs as well as lower upfront costs.

Remember that when taking a certification exam, the vendor is trying to make you a cheerleader for their product. Always lean towards answers that put the product in the best light possible. Amazon isn't going to say bad things about their product in a certification exam.

options.text: Regulatory compliance when laws restrict where data computations can occur

answer:
All of the options listed here, the only valid reason to choose an on-premises deployment would be regulatory compliance rules.

Some countries and provinces have strict rules about moving personal data outside of their borders. If an AWS resource isn't available in that country, AWS would not be a deployment option.

query: Which of the following are standard best-practices for handling AWS IAM accounts?

options.text: Reduce the permissions associated with the root account
Rotate your root access key regularly
Enable multi-factor authentication on your root account
Do not use the root user for everyday tasks

answer:
All of the options here are recommended best practices, with the exception of reducing the permissions associated with the root user account.

It is not possible to reduce the root accounts permissions. That's why it's important to protect the root account as much as possible.

query: Which of the following are valid MFA options in AWS for the root account?

options.text: A virtual MFA device such as software that emulates a physical device
A hardware MFA device that generates a six-digit numeric code based upon a time synchronized algorithm

answer:
Virtual and physical MFA devices, along with a U2F security key or even an SMS text message are valid MFA options.

A strong password is not part of MFA. MFA must supplement the password with something you have. MFA typically means proving you are with something you have and something you know. The password is something you have. An SMS message to your phone proves you also have your phone, providing confidence to the system that you are indeed who you say you are.

query: Which of the following is true about MFA in AWS?

options.text: Only the root account can be configured to use MFA
You can configure MFA for the root account without switching it on for regular IAM users
When MFA is turned on for users, each IAM account uses the same MFA configuration
When MFA is turned on for users, each IAM account has its own MFA configuration

answer:
MFA can be enable only for the root user, or it can be turned on for both the root user and for all regular IAM users as well.

MFA requries 'something you have and something you know.' The thing you know is the password, but the 'thing you have' may be different for each user. As a result, each user will have their own MFA configuration.

query: Key benefits of an Elastic Load Balancer include

options.text: The ability to distribute traffic across EC2 instances in single or multiple availability zones
The ability to perform health checks and route traffic only to EC2 instances that are responsive
The ability to perform load balancing on both public and internal networks
An a ability to scale up EC2 instances when traffic exceeds a specified threshold

answer:
An Elastic Load Balancer cannot spin up new EC2 instances based on traffic patterns.

However, an Elastic Load Balancer can be public or privately facing, it provides high availability, it provides high throughput, does health checks, implements sticky sessions and can be configured with delete protection.

query: Services such as AWS Data Transfer and Amazon S3, have volume pricing tiers across certain usage dimensions that give you lower prices the more you use the service. How can an organization combine usage from multiple accounts in order to move to a cheaper volume pricing tier?

options.text: Change all service usage so that it happens under a single account
Use an elastic load balancer to send all data to services configured under a single account
Set up consolidated billing in AWS Organizations
You cannot combine service usage from multiple accounts to reach a better volume pricing tier

answer: If an organization brings all their users together under an AWS Organization and subsequently signs up for consolidated billing, service usage will be aggregated, which has the potential to make the organization eligible for better volume pricing discounts.

query: Spot instances can be interrupted by AWS with only two minutes worth of notice. As of January 2022, what percentage of running spot instances get stopped by AWS?
answer:
While the fact that AWS can interrupt a Spot Instance with only two minutes worth of notice, the fact is, less than 10% of Spot Instances get stopped by AWS.

Amazon says 92% of Spot Instances are stopped by the customer, which means only 8% of Spot Instances are interrupted by AWS.

You will unlikely be asked about percentages like this on the exam. But it is worth knowing that while Spot Instances can be interrupted, the probability of that happening is fairly rare.

query: What two reasons would cause AWS to reclaim your Spot Instance?

options.text: Your AWS instance successfully completed its work and returned an exit code of 0
Another AWS customer bid a higher amount for the Spot Instance
On Demand or Reserved Instances require the previously spare processing power
The Spot price has risen above your pre-configured maximum Spot price

answer:
There are two scenarios in which AWS will reclaim a Spot Instance.

First, if an On Demand or Reserved Instance requires processing power, your Spot Instance can be interrupted.

Secondly, if the Spot price has risen above your pre-configured maximum Spot price, the Spot Instance will be interrupted.

You can indeed terminate your own Spot Instance at any time, but that is the client decision, not an interruption by AWS. Furthermore, AWS Spot Instances don't work like eBay. They are not provisioned through a bidding war.

query: What is the default behavior when a Spot Instance is interrupted?
answer:
When a Spot instance is interrupted, the default behavior is termination.

You can optionally configure a Spot instance to hibernate or stop upon an interruption, but this is no the default behavior.

There is no pause option for Spot Instances.

As a result, it is recommended to add Spot Instances to your Auto Scaling strategy after your environment has been tested and stabilized.

query: Name two benefits of using Amazon CloudFront in your cloud-based architecture?

options.text: CloudFront can automatically scale EC2 instance when demand increases
Latency is reduced as files are delivered to your clients faster
CloudFront is a free service for AWS customers
The workload on your core infrastructure is reduced

answer:
Amazon CloudFront is not free, nor does it perform autoscaling.

CloudFront caches content on a number of servers across the globe.

Cached content reduced the need for your core infrastructure to handle client requests, which reduces the workload your core servers must handle.

Also, since content is served from locations that are close to where it is being requested, there is less latency, as the content gets delivered faster.

query: Which types of data or files would be good candidates to cache on an Amazon CloudFront Edge location?
answer:
The best candidates for a content cache are ones that change infrequently. As such, HTML, image and audio files are good candidates for content to cache at an Amazon CloudFront Edge location.

Realtime data this is changing constantly is not a good candidate for content caching.

query: How does Amazon CloudFront increase reliability and availability of your content?

options.text: By tracking the number of requests made to your cached content
By increasing the number of Edge locations that host your data when traffic increases
By holding cached duplicates of your content in multiple edge locations around the world
By increasing the number of containers that support your application when load increases

answer: Amazon CloudFront duplicates content throughout the globe. With multiple copies of your content being served from multiple locations, not only is latency lowered, but your content is more available and more reliable. After all, if one Edge server goes offline, your content is still available from other Edge locations around the world.

query: Amazon CloudFront will always:

options.text: Route requests to the Edge location with the lowest time delay
Route requests to an Edge location that already has a copy of data requested
Route requests to the server with the newest copy of the cached data
Will always route requests to the AWS Service that centrally hosts the data requested

answer:
As per the docs, Amazon CloudFront will always request data from the Edge location that has the lowest latency, even if that location does not already have a copy of the cached data. If the cached data is not in the Edge location, the data is then requested from the central server.

This approach to reading cached data is often referred to as lazy-loading.

query: Which of the following is true about Amazon CloudFront?

options.text: The use of Amazon CloudFront decreases network latency while increasing data transfer rates
The use of Amazon CloudFront increases network latency while decreasing data transfer ratesady has a copy of data requested
Amazon CloudFront reduces the number of networks a request must pass through
Amazon CloudFront has no impact on the number networks a request must pass through

answer: As per the docs, Amazon CloudFront can increase the data transfer rate by sending all requests through the AWS backbone. This is much faster than using regular Internet hop points. It also reduced the number of networks a request must move through.

query: Which of the following security best practices does Amazon recommend?

options.text: Do not use the root account for administrative tasks
Only assign one IAM access key per user
Enable multi-factor authentication on the root account

answer:
Amazon recommends against using the root account for any everyday task, including administrative functions.

Amazon also recommends MFA on the root account for added security.

The rotation of access keys is another recommendation. But to do so requires two IAM access keys per account, which makes the assertion users should only ever have one IAM access key incorrect.

query: The rotation of IAM access keys involves:

options.text: Having two IAM access keys for each account
Never having two IAM access keys active at the same time

answer:
Access key rotation is an highly recommended security measure.

According to the docs, IAM access key rotation involves:

  1. The creation of a a second IAM access key in addition to the access key currently being used.
  2. Having an admin update all applications so they use the new IAM access key. Then ensure all applications work properly with the new IAM key. At this point, both IAM access keys are active
  3. Make the older IAM access key inactive
  4. Double check to ensure all of your AWS services and apps are working.
  5. Permanently delete the old, inactive IAM access key.

  3. Make the older IAM access key inactive
  4. Double check to ensure all of your AWS services and apps are working.

query: Which of the following statements is true about the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

options.text: Customer responsibilities are constant across all AWS products
Customer responsibilities may vary with the AWS product being used
AWS is responsible for the security of the cloud
AWS is responsible for security in the cloud

answer:
Customer responsibilities in the Shared Responsibility model will change depending on the product. For example, EC2 users will need to patch their own database engines. RDB users will not.

query: Which of the following are considered customer responsibilities in the AWS Shared Responsibility model?

options.text: Patching the database engine used by DynamoDB
Patching the operating system of an Amazon EC2 instance
The choice of data encryption options
Applying permissions to users with IAM tools

answer:
For a fully managed service like DynamoDB, AWS takes care of database engine patching. However, for EC2 instances, software and OS patches are the responsibility of the client.

The choice of data encryption options and the application of IAM permissions to users is always a customer responsibility.

View the docs for the AWS Shared Responsibility Model.

query: Which of the following are purely customer responsibilities in the AWS Shared Responsibility model?

options.text: Zone Security which may require a customer to route or zone data within specific security environments

answer:
Awareness and training are considered shared controls in Amazon's responsibility model.

Service and Communications Protection or Zone Security which may require a customer to route or zone data within specific security environments are solely the responsibility of the customer based on the application they are deploying.

View the docs for the AWS Shared Responsibility Model.

query: Which of the following statements are true?

options.text: A continent has more Regional Edge Caches than Edge Locations
A continent has more Edge Locations than Regional Edge Caches
A continent will have more Edge Locations than Regions
A continent will have more Regions than Edge Locations

answer:
Regional Edge Caches are the least common part of the AWS Global Infrastructure.

There are more Edge Locations on each continent than there are Regional Edge Caches.

And there are always more Edge Locations than there are AWS Regions in any given continent.

Take a look at the AWS docs for more information on Regions, Zones and Edge Locations.

query: Which of the following statements are true about AWS Regions and Availability Zones?

options.text: An AWS Region is made up of one or more availability zones
An AWS Region is made up of two or more availability zones
Availability Zone within a Region have independent power, cooling, and physical security
Availability Zone within a Region have shared power, cooling, and physical security

answer:
AWS Regions are made up of two or more availability zones, and those separate Availability Zones have independent cooling, power and security. That provides independence between Availability Zones, which provides fault-tolerance within a single region.

query: To deploy a fault-tolerant EC2 instance within a Region:

options.text: Deploy your EC2 instance to the Region and it will automatically switch zones in the event of a failure
Deploy your EC2 instance to multiple Availability Zones within the Region
Deploy your EC2 instance to multiple Availability Zones within the Region and set up a Load Balancer to distribute traffic
You cannot achieve fault tolerance within a Region. Applications must be deployed to multiple Regions for fault tolerance.

answer:
To achieve fault tolerance, deploy to two Availability Zones and use a Load Balancer. The Load Balancer will distribute traffic between the two Zones, while at the same time performing health checks. If one EC2 instance goes offline, all traffic will be routed to the working instance.

Take a look at the AWS docs for more information on Regions, Zones and Edge Locations.

query: Why might an organization choose to replicate data across AWS Regions, rather than simply replicating data between Availability Zones within a region?

options.text: Low latency access across the globe

answer:
While deployment to multiple availability zones within a region provides redundancy and fault tolerance, it is possible to take fault tolerance and redundancy to the next level by deploying to multiple AWS Regions and connecting those Regions with high speed networking connections. Such a configuration has the ability to improve response times around the globe, although Edge locations would likely be a cheaper alternative.

Indubitably, deployment across multiple regions will not be a cost savings endeavor, making he suggestion of a lower overall AWS cost an incorrect answer.

Take a look at the AWS docs for more information on Regions, Zones and Edge Locations.

Apply permissions to users and add users to groups

query: If a new user joins your organization and requires full administrative access, how should you proceed?

options.text: Provide the new user with the root username and password
Provide the new user with the root user's access and secret keys
Use the root account to add the user to an IAM group that has administrative privledges
Use a non-root account to add the user to an IAM group that has administrative privledges

answer:
There are close to zero scenarios where providing a new user with root level credentials is the right thing to do.

If a new user requires administrative access, simply add that user to a group with administrative access.

Note that even for operations that assign other users permissions, you should never use the root account. Use another non-root account that has permissions to manage users.

query: A member of the finance department's IT team has joined the company's DevOps team, which requires a new set of rights assignments for the user. What is the best way to achieve this?

options.text: Delete the user's old IAM account. Then create a new IAM account and apply new IAM permissions to the account.
Delete the user's old IAM account. Then create a new IAM account add this account to the appropriate IAM group.
Remove all the finance departments rights on the account, and then add new rights that apply to the DevOps department
Remove the user from the finance department's IAM group and add the account to the DevOps group

answer:
User rights and policies should be assigned to groups, and then users get added to those groups, subsequently inheriting all of the rights and policies associated with the group.

There is no need to delete an IAM account when it comes to switching permissions.

query: Which of the following statements are true about IAM groups and roles?

options.text: Users can belong to muptiple IAM groups
A user can only belong to one IAM group
A permission applied to a group applies to all users in that group
A permission applied to a user also applies to all other users in the groups to which they belong

answer:
Users can belong to multiple groups. A user then becomes subject to all of the permissions and policies applies across all of the groups to which they belong.

Permission applied to a single user do not apply to the other users in the groups to which they belong. User level permissions apply only to the user to whom the are applied.

query: Which of the following statements are true about Identity and Access Management username requirements?

options.text: IAM usernames cannot contain a plus sign (+) or comma ( , )
Email addresses cannot be used as IAM usernames
IAM usernames are not case sensitive
IAM usernames can be any Unicode character

answer:
IAM usernames may contain any ASCII character, which means emojis and other characters unique to the Unicode character set are not allows.

IAM usernames can include special characters such as a plus (+), equal (=), comma (,), period (.), at (@), underscore (_), and hyphen (-). Since the @ sign is allowed, emails are completely valid IAM usernames.

Check the AWS Identity Management userguide for more details.

IAM usernames are not case sensitive. You can't have two accounts where one is named BOB and the other is named Bob.

query: Which of the following statements are true about IAM quotas as of January 1st, 2022?

options.text: A non-root, IAM user can be assigned a maximum of 2 access keys
The AWS root account can be assigned an unlimited number of access keys
An IAM user can be a member of a maximum of 10 IAM group
There is no practical limit on the number of groups and IAM user can be a part of

answer:
There's no need to know the exact quota numbers for various IAM entities. It's unlikely you'll need to know that 10 is the maximum number of groups to which a user can be assigned.

However, what is important is understanding there are quota limits. You don't need to know the exact quota numbers. What you do need to know is that there are quotas and limits assigned to a variety of IAM entities.

For the exam, you do need to know that IAM users, including the root user, can be assigned a maximum of 2 access keys. The reason for this is to be able to perform access key rotation. Access key rotation is one of the AWS Practitioner Exam objectives: 2.3 Access keys and password policies (rotation, complexity).

You can read more about access quotas in the docs.

query: Which of the following statements are true about IAM quotas as of January 1st, 2022?

options.text: IAM does not support nested groups
Nested groups is a key differentiating feature of IAM
To assign a permission to every account, assign a permission to the default EVERYONE group, and every user inherits that permission
There is no default user group that includes all users in your AWS account

answer:
IAM does not support nested groups. Any administrator that has ever had to deal with nested groups is very happy with that user management limitation.

There is no default EVERYONE group in AWS. If you want to have a single group that all users are a part of, you need to create that group yourself.

You can read more about access quotas in the docs.

query: Which of the following statements conform to Amazon best practices with regards to the AWS root account?

options.text: You should delete the access keys for the AWS root user
You should never delete the access keys for the AWS root user
You should protect the root account with multi-factor authentication (MFA)
The root account credentials should only ever be used in secure, server-side applications

answer:
Amazon suggests deleting the AWS root user's access keys. Access keys are used for CLI functions and APIs, and you shouldn't be doing those things with the root account!

MFA is definitely a best practice for the root account.

And the root account should never be used in an application, even if it's a server-side app. Create a group with special permissions if such a function is required. Never use the root account in an app.

You can read more about root access best practices in the docs.

query: To limit access to a specific IP address, an S3 bucket policy would need to include:
answer:
A condition makes it possible to perform additional functions within a bucket policy, such as blocking a range of IP addresses.

Here is an example of a Condition added to a bucket policy:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Id": "S3PolicyId9",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "IPAllow",
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:*",
      "Resource": [
	       "arn:aws:s3:::DROP-IN-THE-BUCKET",
         "arn:aws:s3:::DROP-IN-THE-BUCKET/*"
      ],
      "Condition": {
	 "NotIpAddress": {"aws:SourceIp": "22.192.168.10/12"}
      }
    }
  ]
}

You can read more in the bucket policy in the FAQ.

query: To forbid a particular URL or domain name from accessing content made publicly available, you would add this to your S3 Bucket policy
answer:
A condition makes it possible to perform additional functions within a bucket policy, such as blocking a given domain from accessing your content.

Here is an example of a Condition added to a bucket policy:

{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Id":"S3 Bucket HTTP Restriction example",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Sid":"S3 Bucket Example of Denying Access to a WebSite",
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":"*",
      "Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:GetObjectVersion"],
      "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::DROP-IN-THE-S3-BUCKET/*",
      "Condition":{
        "StringLike":{"aws:Referer":["http://www.mcnz.com/*","http://scrumtuous.com/*"]}
      }
    }
  ]
}

You can read more in the bucket policy in the FAQ.

query: An S3 Bucket Policy can be used to:

options.text: Force users to access S3 content through CloudFront only
Load balance S3 content between availability zones
Block URLs and IP addresses from accessing bucket content

answer:
An S3 Bucket Policy does not perform autoscaling, implement elasticity or provide fault-tolerance functions.

However, forcing users to use CloudFront Edge locations, requiring MFA and blocking IP addresses and domains from accessing S3 Bucket content are all functions a Bucket Policy can perform.

You can read more in the bucket policy in the FAQ.

query: This AWS product allows customers to run AWS infrastructure and services on-premises for a consistent hybrid experience?
answer:
AWS Outposts allows you to run AWS infrastructure and services on premises for a consistent hybrid experience.

AWS Wavelength embeds AWS compute and storage services at the edge of 5G networks for a faster application response time.

AWS Local Zones put AWS services near large population and industry centers so you can reach local users in milliseconds.

AWS Snow devices collect and process data between the edge and AWS so that your apps run in all conditions.

AWS Outposts, Wavelength, Local Zones and Snow are all categorized as Amazon services that help empower hybrid cloud computing.

Learn more in the AWS FAQ.

query: To assist in the analysis and querying of AWS Cost and Usage Reports, Amazon suggests integration with which product?
answer:
Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. You can configure Amazon Athena with CUR when you do the initial setup. When setting up an AWS Cost & Usage report, you can select the option to integrate with Amazon Athena.

You can learn more in the AWS Cost and Usage Report docs.

query: You need to immediate launch an EC2 instance that will be in service for an extended period of time. But you also know the operating system used will likely change in the near future. Which type of Reserved Instance should you purchase?
answer:
The Convertible Reserved Instance is the correct answer.

The key to this question is the fact that you need to switch, or covert, from one OS to another in the near future. You can't do this with a Standard Reserved Instance, but it is possible with a Convertible Reserved Instance.

query: The reason why services such as Amazon DynamoDB encrypt data at rest by default is:

options.text: Increase the speed of data transmission over SSL
Assist in the generation of digital certificates
Ensure that data is secure, right down to the storage system
If there is ever a systems breach, hackers would not be able to read the data they obtained

answer:
Encrypting data, even the data that sits securely on the hard drive (aka data at rest), is a well proven best practice for securing data.

By encrypting data at rest, even if the data found its way into the hands of a hacker or theif, the data would be unreadable in its encrypted state.

You can learn more about Amazon's DynamoDB in the docs.

query: Which of the following is not true about DynamoDB

options.text: DynamoDB supports key-value pair data models
DynamoDB supports server-side ACID compliant transactions
DynamoDB supports document type data models

answer:
Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database that supports key-value and document data models.

Furthermore, Amazon's DynamoDB brags that it provides native, server-side support for transactions, simplifying the developer experience of making coordinated, all-or-nothing changes to multiple items both within and across tables.

You can learn more about Amazon's DynamoDB in the docs.

answer:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB captures item-level changes in your DynamoDB tables as a Kinesis data stream. This feature enables you to build advanced streaming applications such as real-time log aggregation, real-time business analytics, and Internet of Things data capture.

You can learn more about Amazon's DynamoDB in the docs.

query: The following are compelling features of Amazon DynamoDB that set it apart from competitive offerings:

options.text: On-demand backup and restore operations that run with no impact on performance
Full support for the ANSI SQL-87 standard
Default encryption for all data at rest

answer:
Amazon DynamoDB supports encryption of all data at rest, point-in-time recovery, and zero-impact backup operations.

However, DynamoDB is a NoSQL database. It does not support the Structured Query Language standard.

You can learn more about Amazon's DynamoDB in the docs.

query: The opposite of 'data in use' or 'data in transit' is:
answer:
One of the Practitioner Exam objectives is to understand various encryption options for data in transit and data at rest. Understanding that objective means understanding what data at rest actually is.

Data at rest is any data that is currently saved on a hard drive somewhere and not actively being used. AWS services like DynamoDB encrypt data at rest by default, so that if anyone ever stole a hard drive, or somehow got access to the data, they would be unable to read it, as it would be encrypted and undecipherable.

Here is the AWS Practitioner Exam Objective on 'data at rest:' Identify different encryption options on AWS (for example, In transit, At rest)

You can learn more about Amazon's DynamoDB in the docs.

query: A feature or service made available through the AWS Management Console is available through the AWS CLI interface:

options.text: On the same day the service is made available through the AWS Management Console
Within 90 days of the service being made available through the AWS Management Console
Within 180 days of the service being made available through the AWS Management Console
Services available in the AWS Management Console are not accessible through the AWS CLI

answer:
Anything you can do through the AWS Management Console can be done through the AWS CLI. Sometimes, when a new feature arrives, there may be a short delay in that service being available through the CLI, but Amazon promises that delay will never be more than 180 days.

All IaaS (infrastructure as a service) AWS administration, management, and access functions in the AWS Management Console are available in the AWS API and AWS CLI. New AWS IaaS features and services provide full AWS Management Console functionality through the API and CLI at launch or within 180 days of launch.

The real takeaway is that anything you can do through the console, you can do it through the CLI, and vice versa.

Learn more about AWS SDKs in their docs.

query: Failover and fault tolerance can be fully achieved through the use of only two Availability Zones (AZ) because:

options.text: Each AZ has its own independent power supply garnered through separate substations
Each AZ has it's own independent and isolated hardware
No two AZs are less than 100km apart to mitigate against natural disasters
AZs are always located in lower risk flood plains.

answer:
AZs are never more than 100km apart. This is a requirement in order to keep latency between the two AZs as low as possible.

Every other point about AZs is true. You only need to load balance across two AZs to be fully fault tolerant.

query: Which of the following services, when connected to an EC2 instance, acts almost like a USB drive connected to a desktop computer?
answer:
Amazon's Elastic Block Storage acts very much like a USB drive attached to a laptop or desktop. An Amazon EBS volume is a durable, block-level storage device that you can attach to your instances. After you attach a volume to an instance, you can use it as you would use a physical hard drive. EBS volumes are flexible.

Learn more about EBS in the docs.

query: Which of the following are industry differentiating features of Amazon EBS volumes?

options.text: The ability to dynamically change the volume type on live production volumes
The ability to format the EBS volume without losing data
The ability to dynamically modify the provisioned IOPS capacity
The ability to increase volume size dynamically

answer:
You cannot format an EBS volume without losing data. But the other options are all valid for EBS.

For current-generation volumes attached to current-generation instance types, you can dynamically increase size, modify the provisioned IOPS capacity, and change volume type on live production volumes.

query: Which of the following statements are true about Amazon EBS volumes connected to an EC2 instance?

options.text: When an EC2 instance goes offline, so does the associated EBS volume
When an EBS volume goes offline, so does the associated EC2 instance
EC2 instances stop and start independently of EBS volumes
EBS volumes stop and start independently of EC2 intances

answer:
EBS volumes persist independently from the running life of an EC2 instance.

EC2 instances stop and start independently of EBS volumes, and vice versa.

Learn more about Amazon EBS in the docs.

An EBS volume can be attached to multiple EC2 instances at a time

query: The recommended storage option when you run a database on an instance is:

options.text: The file system of the EC2 instance

answer:
For persistence beyond the life of the EC2 instance, you want to use Amazon EBS.

Here's what Amazon says: Amazon EBS provides durable, block-level storage volumes that you can attach to a running instance. You can use Amazon EBS as a primary storage device for data that requires frequent and granular updates. For example, Amazon EBS is the recommended storage option when you run a database on an instance.

query: Which of the following is true about Amazon EBS?

options.text: You can detach and EBS from one EC2 instance and then attach it to a different EC2 instance
An EBS volume can be attached to any EC2 instance in the same Region
An EBS volume can be attached to multiple EC2 instances at the same time
An EC2 instance can be attached to multiple EBS volumes at the same time

answer:
The only incorrect assertion here about Amazon EBS is the idea that EBS volume has Regional scope. That is not correct. An EBS volume has AZ scope. The EC2 instance an EBS connects to has to be in the same Availability Zone, not the same AWS Region.

All the other options are correct.

Learn more about Amazon EBS in the docs.

query: You need to create a database instance within the Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS). What three options are available to you?

options.text: Use the CreateDBInstance object in the AWS API for RDS

answer:
There are always at least three ways to create, configure and manage resources in AWS:

  • The AWS Management Console
  • The Command Line Interface
  • The AWS API

You won't need to know any specific commands or API objects on the AWS Practitioner Certification Exam. However, you will need to know the three approaches to AWS resource management.

Here's what Amazon says in their docs: You can create a DB instance using the console, the create-db-instance CLI command, or the CreateDBInstance RDS AWS API operation.

query: Which of the following statements are true about AWS Beanstalk and AWS CloudFormation?

options.text: Behind the scenes, Elastic Beanstalk uses CloudFormation to create and maintain resources
Behind the scenes, CloudFormation uses Elastic Beanstalk to create and maintain resources.
Elastic Beanstalk is a more managed service than CloudFormation
CloudFormation  is a more managed service than Elastic Beanstalk

answer:
I think this is an advanced question for the AWS Practitioner exam, and could very well be beyond scope.

Elastic Beanstalk is a highly managed solution that requires very little administration or involvement. That's why we love it. It's a managed service.

AWS CloudFormation is more hands on. It requires more input and insight from the AWS user, so it is less of a managed service than Elastic Beanstalk.

According to AWS, behind the scenes, Elastic Beanstalk uses CloudFormation to create and maintain resources.

Read more in the AWS CloudFormation docs docs.

query: Which of the following statements are true about CloudFormation?

options.text: Anything you can do with the AWS CLI you can do with CloudFormation
Anything you can do through the AWS Management Console can be done with CloudFormation
Anything you can do through the AWS SDKs can be done with CloudFormation
CloudFormation cannot manage the same set of AWS resources that the AWS CLI can

answer:
According to Amazon, AWS CloudFormation offers an easy and consistent way to model, provision, and manage a collection of related AWS and third-party resources. However, CloudFormation only provides management options for a subset of AWS services. CloudFormation does not promise to be able to configure every AWS resource in existence. In contrast, AWS promises all objects to be configurable through the CLI within 180 days of the resource being released to the public.

Read more in the AWS CloudFormation docs docs.

query: Which of the following statements are true about VPCs?

options.text: Every VPC needs at least one public IP address
A VPC can be configured without any public IP addresses
EC2 instances in your VPC require a public IP addresses to communicate with resources in the service.
EC2 nstances in your VPC do not require public IP addresses to communicate with resources in the service.

answer:
VPC do not need a public IP address.

Furthermore, Traffic between your VPC and the other service does not leave the Amazon network.

This definition is from Amazon: VPC endpoint — Enables you to privately connect your VPC to supported AWS services and VPC endpoint services powered by PrivateLink without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or AWS Direct Connect connection.

You can learn more about Amazon VPCs in the docs.

A Network ACL is an optional VPC security layer
A Network ACL can allow or deny traffic
A Network ACL can allow but not deny traffic

Every VPC needs to be associated with at least one Security Group
Every VPC needs to be associated with at least one Network ACL

query: Which of the following is not true about AWS Direct Connect?

options.text: AWS Direct Connect allows you to create virtual interfaces directly to the AWS cloud
AWS Direct Connect connections bypass your Internet service provider
AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated network connection between your on-premises network and AWS
AWS Direct Connect can only connect to VPNs with a public IP address

answer:
All of the options are true except for the fact that a public IP address is required for an AWS Direct Connect connection. AWS Direct Connect can connect to a VPN through an endpoint, which does not require a public ip address .

You can learn more about AWS Direct Connect in the docs.

query: AWS Config is often integrated with which popular 3rd Party tools?
answer:

The AWS Practitioner Exam Objectives ask users to know about some 3rd party tools. And these details about JIRA and ServiceNow are in the AWS Config User Docs. However, my hunch is that knowledge about ServiceNow and JIRA integration would be outside the scope of the exam.

query: Which of the following statements are true about AWS Config?

options.text: AWS Config will report non-compliance configurations after they happen
AWS Config will prevent non-compliance configurations from being applied
AWS Config will lock a user's account if too many non-compliant configurations are attempted
AWS Config will rollback a non-compliant configuration to its previously compliant state

answer:
AWS Config can't prevent a user from configuring an AWS resource in a non-compliant manner. All AWS Config can do is report back whenever it audits a resource and finds to be out of compliance.

Note that an exam objective demands test takers know that auditing and reporting services exist: Recognize there are services that will aid in auditing and reporting. A sub-requirement lists CloudWatch, AWS Config and CloudTrail. Define Amazon CloudWatch, AWS Config, and AWS CloudTrail

You can learn more about AWS Config in the docs.

query: Which of the following are true about the manner in which Amazon CloudWatch allows users to consume logs for auditing and monitoring purposes?

options.text: CloudWatch allows you to monitor logs in real time
CloudWatch allows you to set an alarm on the number of errors that occur in your system logs
CloudWatch allows you to view graphs of latency of web requests from your application logs
Amazon CloudWatch will store your log files for up to a maximum of 365 days (one year)

answer:
Amazon says CloudWatch allows you to monitor logs in almost real time.

Also, you can configure a low-cost S3 bucket to store your CloudWatch log files for as long as you like. There is no limit on how long you can retain your CloudWatch log files for.

query: The use of a managed database service like Amazon Aurora eliminates the need for you to:

options.text: Pay employees to install database software on a computer
Pay licensing fees for the use of the Amazon Aurora database
Perform database maintenance and apply security patches
Pay employees to create database tables and entity relationship diagrams (ERDs)

answer:
When you use a managed service like Amazon Aurora, you no longer have labor costs related to paying employees to install database software, perform maintenance, or even negotiate license fees. That's all part of the cloud value proposition.

However, you will still need to figure out how your data is structured, which means having employees figure out what tables you need and create ERDs when they are done.

query: This relational database offering is said to be faster and more scalable than Amazon RDS:
answer:
DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, not a relational database.

Amazon Redshift is used for data warehousing.

DB2 running on EC2 would not run as fast as Amazon RDS, although the people at IBM might disagree.

Amazon Aurora is a relational database offering that has a much different architecture from Amazon RDS, and as a result, runs faster and is more scalable than Amazon RDS.

Amazon Aurora is not listed in the AWS Practitioner Exam Objectives, but it is listed as a tool or technology that could appear on the exam.

Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS are both relational databases
Both Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS support MySQL and PostgreSQL
Both Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS support Oracle Database and SQL Server

Both Amazon Aurora and RDS are relational database offerings. But Aurora only supports MySQL and PostgreSQL.

Amazon Aurora is not listed in the AWS Practitioner Exam Objectives, but it is listed as a tool or technology that could appear on the exam.

query: Which of the following databases engines does Amazon RDS support?
answer:
Amazon RDS does not support IBM DB2.

Note that Amazon RDS supports more database engines than Amazon Aurora, which is another Amazon relational database. Amazon RDS is available on several database instance types - optimized for memory, performance or I/O - and provides you with six familiar database engines to choose from, including Amazon Aurora, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle Database, and SQL Server.

Amazon Aurora is not listed in the AWS Practitioner Exam Objectives, but it is listed as a tool or technology that could appear on the exam.

query: How are tags used in cost allocation?

options.text: Cost allocation tags help you organize and categorize expenditures
Cost allocation tags help make AWS Cost and Usage Reports easier to understand
Cost allocation tags stop resources from exceeding their allocated budgets
Cost allocation tags can help organizations with large budgets break down costs in a more meaningful way

query: When should a relational database solution, such as RDS or Aurora, be chosen over Amazon S3 storage?

options.text: When you need to form relationships between stored data
When a structure language is needed to query and search for data
When data needs to be accessed through a key-value pair approach
When the data is created, fetched and updated rapidly

answer: Amazon S3 is a great service for key-value based object storage. But it doesn't replace a relational database like Aurora or RDS when you need relationships between objects, you need to query your data in a complex way, and the data may be subject to read and write operations that require low latency transactional facilities.

query: You have a number of largely static websites hosted in the Oregon region. However, your users in India complain about slow page load times. What technologies could you use to reduce latency and make your users in India happy?

options.text: Put static content into Amazon S3 buckets
Force all S3 requests to go through CloudFront
Force Amazon S3 requests to be served through Edge locations

answer: If you want to speed up the delivery of static content, put that content into Amazon S3 buckets, turn on Amazon CloudFront, and then force all Amazon S3 requests to be served through an Edge location that caches the static content.

query: What is the name of Amazon's highly available and scalable Domain Name System (DNS)?
answer:
Route 53 is Amazon's DNS web service.

Amazon Route 53 effectively connects user requests to infrastructure running in AWS – such as Amazon EC2 instances, Elastic Load Balancing load balancers, or Amazon S3 buckets – and can also be used to route users to infrastructure outside of AWS.

Learn more in the Route 45 docs.

query: Your S3 bucket names needs to be unique, so you decide to use the email addresses as the root of the bucket name. Which of the following options would be valid S3 bucket names?
answer:
An S3 bucket name cannot use a Unix slash, DOS slash, or the @ sign.

Here are more details on what can and cannot go into an S3 bucket name.

  • Bucket names must be between 3 and 63 characters long.

  • Bucket names can consist only of lowercase letters, numbers, dots (.), and hyphens (-).

  • Bucket names must begin and end with a letter or number.

  • Bucket names must not be formatted as an IP address (for example, 192.168.5.4).

  • Bucket names must not start with the prefix xn--.

  • Bucket names must not end with the suffix -s3alias. This suffix is reserved for access point alias names. For more information, see Using a bucket-style alias for your access point.

  • Bucket names must be unique within a partition. A partition is a grouping of Regions. AWS currently has three partitions: aws (Standard Regions), aws-cn (China Regions), and aws-us-gov (AWS GovCloud [US] Regions).

  • Buckets used with Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration can't have dots (.) in their names. For more information about Transfer Acceleration, see Configuring fast, secure file transfers using Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.

options.text: Across all users of the IAM account

Turning off 'Block all public access' and adding a permissive ACL control will make content in an S3 bucket publicly accessible on the Internet

However, the object owner can optionally share objects with others by creating a presigned URL, using their own security credentials, to grant time-limited permission to download the objects.

query: The effect of the AWS policy shown in code would be to:

options.text: Allow anyone in the principal group to view the jfif file
Allow anyone to view the jfif file
Allow anyone in the principal group to view, edit or delete the file
Allow anyone to perform any operation on the jfif file

answer:
The "s3:*" action is a dangerous action to allow in an S3 Bucket policy, because it references every possible action on a object.

The effect on this policy is allow, the "*" wildcard indicates the permission applies to everyone, and the s3:* action means any operation is allowed. So anyone can perform any operation they want on the jfif file.

query: You have written an S3 policy in JSON, but the code won't compile because of a missing comma, square brace or bracket. Which online tool could help you identify the problem?
answer:
Checking the basic syntax of your code is called 'linting.' To fine JSON errors, I often use jsonlint

There are various online lint tools for XML, JSON, HTML, YAML and other languages.

If you've messed up something in your JSON, paste your code into a linting tool. It might help you identify the problem.

Just be sure never to put anything private or confidential into an online linting tool.

query: A startup that uses the AWS cloud for all of their infrastructure and service needs experiences which benefit:

options.text: The ability to focus more efforts on product development
The ability to focus more efforts on revenue generating activities
The ability to gain skills in managing hardware
The elimination of the need to monitor costs

answer:
The use of the AWS cloud allows users to focus on business value and not having to deal with infrastructure tasks such as managing servers, upgrading processors or adding a new hard drive to a compute. As a result, businesses can focus on creative tasks, product development and hopefully revenue generation.

Use of the cloud will not enhance an organizations understanding of hardware or infrastructure. And even though the cloud is being used, costs must still be monitored. Operating in the cloud can indeed get expensive.

answer:
"If you store 10,000 objects in S3, you may lose on every 10 million years or so." That is how reliable S3 storage is.

Note that reliability is different from availability. Availability is an indication of how accessible an object is. The data in S3 may be stored durably, but that doesn't mean the service may go offline from time to time and your objects, while stored reliably, might not be available for a moment or two.

query: Expensive mistakes made purchasing hardware to meet the capacity of unpredictable workloads can be eliminated through the use of Amazon's
answer:
Elasticity provided by AWS allows applications to scale up and and down automatically as workload demands increase and decrease.

By paying only for what you use, organizations can avoid spending millions on hardware and infrastructure expenses that may not be needed if product demand is below expectations.

From the Six Advantages of Cloud Computing: Stop guessing capacity – Eliminate guessing on your infrastructure capacity needs. When you make a capacity decision prior to deploying an application, you often end up either sitting on expensive idle resources or dealing with limited capacity. With cloud computing, these problems go away. You can access as much or as little capacity as you need, and scale up and down as required with only a few minutes’ notice.

query: Amazon's ability to achieve lower variable costs due to their immense size and specialization in IT is known as:
answer:
When an organization achieves incredibly low variable costs through expansion and specialization, it is known as an economy of scale.

From the Six Advantages of Cloud Computing: Benefit from massive economies of scale – By using cloud computing, you can achieve a lower variable cost than you can get on your own. Because usage from hundreds of thousands of customers is aggregated in the cloud, providers such as AWS can achieve higher economies of scale, which translates into lower pay as-you-go prices.

query: The ability for developers to get new test servers spun up, or new NoSQL database instances provisioned quickly, rather than having to wait for on premise ITOps to go through a long requisition process is an example of:

options.text: The benefit of a microservice architecture

answer:
The ability to provision resources quickly when needed so that developers can innovate is known as agility.

From the Six Advantages of Cloud Computing: Increase speed and agility – In a cloud computing environment, new IT resources are only a click away, which means that you reduce the time to make those resources available to your developers from weeks to just minutes. This results in a dramatic increase in agility for the organization, since the cost and time it takes to experiment and develop is significantly lower.

query: The AWS cloud reduces an organizations burden to meet compliance requirements by:

options.text: Inheriting existing ISO 9001 and other industry certifications AWS already has
Through the use of reporting tools that already track every management console operation
Access to AWS Artifact, a tool that generates customizable compliance audit reports
No longer being subject to compliance requirements

answer:
Even if an organization outsources their infrastructure to AWS, they are still responsible for being compliant with industry and government regulations.

Fortunately, AWS makes it easier to meet compliance requirements than if you had an on-premise implementation. AWS is already compliant with many industry standards. You inherit these certifications when you use AWS.

Also, AWS has many tools that track configuration changes, making it possible to easily track and report on changes that happen in your environment.

And perhaps the most helpful tool for meeting compliance requirements is AWS artifact that has over 2500 customizations that allow AWS users to aggregate compliance-related data that is important to you and your partners.

query: Which of the following are benefits of the ability to programmatically automate the provisioning of resources in AWS:

options.text: Automations are cost effective as they do not require human intervention to run them
Automations can take advantage of pay-as-you-go pricing
Problems can be quickly identified and remedied

answer:
There is nothing inherently special about an automation in terms of pay-as-you-go pricing.

However, automation are cost effective as they run without having to pay a human to perform the same task. If they are not working properly, they can be easily inspected and fixed, as their course of actions are well defined. They do not involve problems like forgetfulness or laziness that can happen with a human actor. And they are predictable and repeatable, which is what DevOps professionals like to see in the data center.

query: The term BYOL refers to:
answer:
BYOL stands for Bring Your Own License

For organizations who have already bought a license for a piece of software, AWS provides a number of ways to use that license in the cloud, often through dedicated instances, dedicates machines or some other vendor negotiated solution that works in the cloud.

query: Rental costs associated storing data archives in a secure, off-site location would be an example of:
answer: Rental costs are known as operational expenditures, or OpEx. When organizations move their infrastructure to the cloud, many OpEx and CapEx costs are reduced, if not completely eliminated altogether.
